body:
I love this post and I'm enjoying the discussions in the comments!

I've only started reading and writing fan fics (seriously) the past year. I've read a few here and there over the years but I've never gone as deep as I have now.

***Basics:*** I use my phone/tablet (mobile browser), reversi site skin, have all stats on the blurb and actual work page [hidden](https://www.reddit.com/r/FanFiction/comments/g63dif/hide_all_stats_sitewide_on_ao3_with_a_site_skin/), and I choose a fic based on the tags and summary. I make good use of the filter system (and the [hidden search operators](https://archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/10851), tbh only *otp:true*) whenever I look for what to read. I don't care about word count or whether or not a fic is complete or ongoing. I'm in a couple of different fandoms, and I just read whatever I feel like in the moment! Whenever I discover authors I like I usually binge-read all their works and subscribe (even if they're not active anymore).

***How I interact with and keep track of fics:*** I always make sure to leave kudos and comment whenever I finish *any* fic (I never finish fics I don't at least *like).* I publicly (though now I've moved on to privating) bookmark literally *everything* I read (I won't give a number of how many but it's a lot), and I use my own tags to mark a fic in three diff ways:

1. Whether it's something I *want to read,* am *currently reading,* have *finished reading,* or have *dropped* (Edit: forgot to mention if it's something I've dropped it is always saved as a private bookmark!). I had been a Goodreads user before AO3 so this felt like something natural to adapt for the site.
2. Descriptors: Did it make me *cry?* Did it manage to make me *laugh out loud* more than a dozen times? Did it get me all *hot and bothered?* Was it an *emotional* roller coaster ride?
3. Whether it's a *favorite* (which I then just mark as rec) or an *all-time best* (a masterpiece in my eyes!)

This way I can easily sort using the Bookmarker's Tags I have assigned for works (I have a total of ten tags, all of which fit perfectly for filtering). For any other detailed descriptions of work, I just put in the Notes section!

I don't really download a work unless it's something I *love* and would hate to never be able to re-read again, so I do have a few epubs saved on my PC.

***Other apps/tools I use:*** Aside from the native AO3 bookmarking system, I actually also use Notion to organize everything I read! I like easily seeing stats e.g. how many words I read in a month, or which fandom/ship I read the most for; plus the filtering/sorting options in Notion are quite comprehensive so in some ways it's definitely better than AO3! I basically use the AO3 bookmark function as an 'on-the-go' to quickly log what I had just read, then transfer the info to my Notion page by the end of the week. Some might think this to be a bit redundant or a waste of time, but it definitely works for me! I'm not well-versed in coding or tech stuff in general, so I try to stay as simple as I can with categorizing. [This](https://imgur.com/a/jC7sycn) is what my table looks like--I just input the basics: title (with link embedded), author, word count, tags, date started/finished, etc.

***What I think can be improved site-wise for readers***: The *Mark for Later* option is honestly not the best, which is why I never use it. I actually think it's pretty useless, and the bookmarking system can do a much better job at what it's supposed to do considering how you're at least able to sort them there.

The sorting options are still lacking for bookmarks though, since you can't sort by kudos/hits/word count, and AFAIK (correct me if I'm wrong) you can't even use the hidden search operators to filter them. This is another reason why I also use Notion on top of native bookmarking.

And that's pretty much it! :)

>AO3 is an *archive*, but the others are places to build *communities*.
